newsitem.title: USA: Negotiations to resume in UPS strike.
newsitem.headline: Negotiations to resume in UPS strike.

text.p: The striking Teamsters union will resume contract talks with United Parcel Service on Thursday, the union said on Wednesday.
"We're going to meet with them tomorrow afternoon," a Teamsters spokeswoman said.
A spokesman for the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service said that no time had been set for the meeting.

"Both sides agreed to show up," the spokesman said. "We don't have a specific time yet and we don't know who will be here." The meeting in Washington was called by John Calhoun Wells, who heads the mediation service, the spokesman said.
UPS and the Teamsters have been under pressure from the White House to resume negotiations, which broke off Sunday night leading to the strike that began early Monday.

With UPS handling less than 10 percent of its normal shipments, the strike has meant rising shipping costs and logistical nightmares for businesses, manufacturers and consumers who rely on the the nation's largest package delivery company.
On Tuesday, Labour Secretary Alexis Herman urged UPS Chief Executive James Kelly and Teamster President Ron Carey to go back to the bargaining table.
